subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to Sexual Assault Prevention and Response (SAPR) questions — restricted vs. unrestricted reporting and bystander intervention, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: SAPR Training Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free SAPR (Sexual Assault Prevention & Response) quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Restricted vs. unrestricted reporting, SARC/Victim Advocate roles, bystander intervention.
whyItWorks: SAPR questions often hinge on exactly which reporting option preserves confidentiality and who is authorized to receive that information without breaking it — small differences in wording change the correct answer. Cambo reads the exact scenario on your screen and explains which reporting path applies and why, not just which option to pick.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the primary difference between Restricted and Unrestricted Reporting under the SAPR program?
options: Restricted Reporting allows a victim to confidentially disclose a sexual assault without triggering an official investigation or command notification; Unrestricted Reporting triggers both
Restricted Reporting is only available to officers, while Unrestricted Reporting is available to everyone
Restricted Reporting requires a written statement, while Unrestricted Reporting can be made verbally
There is no meaningful difference — both options result in the same investigative process
sampleQuestions.a: Restricted Reporting lets an eligible victim confidentially access medical care and support services without triggering an official investigation or notifying command, while Unrestricted Reporting notifies command and initiates a law enforcement investigation.

sampleQuestions.q: A service member reports a sexual assault to a SARC and elects Restricted Reporting. Which of the following can she also disclose the details to without converting her report to Unrestricted?
options: Her unit commander
The military police on duty
A Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Victim Advocate or healthcare personnel involved in her care
Any coworker she trusts
sampleQuestions.a: A SAPR Victim Advocate and healthcare personnel providing her care are among the specified individuals who can receive a Restricted Report without it becoming Unrestricted — disclosing to command or law enforcement generally converts the report.

sampleQuestions.q: Why can't a Restricted Report be converted back to Restricted once it has become Unrestricted?
options: Because once command and/or law enforcement have been notified, the confidentiality protections that define Restricted Reporting no longer apply
Because Restricted Reporting is only available for the first 24 hours after an assault
Because a victim can only choose a reporting option once in their entire career
Because Unrestricted Reports are automatically classified
sampleQuestions.a: Once command and/or law enforcement have been notified, the investigative and notification process is already underway — the confidentiality that defines Restricted Reporting can't be restored after that point, which is why a victim can convert Restricted to Unrestricted but not the reverse.

sampleQuestions.q: At a unit function, you notice a visibly intoxicated coworker being led away alone by someone displaying predatory behavior. What does SAPR bystander intervention training call for?
options: Assume someone else will step in if it's really a problem
Wait until the next morning to mention it to your supervisor
Take safe, appropriate action to intervene — directly, or by distracting the situation or enlisting others to help
Do nothing unless you witness an assault actually occurring
sampleQuestions.a: Take safe, appropriate action — bystander intervention training emphasizes acting before a situation escalates, whether that's directly stepping in, creating a distraction, or getting others involved, rather than assuming someone else will handle it.

sampleQuestions.q: What is the role of a Sexual Assault Response Coordinator (SARC)?
options: To determine whether a reported assault actually occurred before support services are provided
To oversee case management and coordinate the victim's access to support services, regardless of which reporting option they choose
To represent the accused in any resulting legal proceeding
To handle only Unrestricted Reports, referring Restricted Reports elsewhere
sampleQuestions.a: A SARC oversees case management and coordinates a victim's access to support services and care, and this role applies whether the victim has chosen Restricted or Unrestricted Reporting.

sampleQuestions.q: Who is eligible to make a Restricted Report under the DoD SAPR program?
options: Only active-duty service members
Any civilian employee, with no age restriction
Service members and their military dependents who are 18 years of age or older
Only personnel who report the assault within 24 hours of it occurring
sampleQuestions.a: Restricted Reporting is available to service members and their military dependents who are 18 or older — it's specifically designed to give adult victims a confidential path to care without an immediate investigation.

faqs.q: How often is SAPR training required?
faqs.a: Annually for all service members DoD-wide, with additional training typically required at accession, before deployment, and for personnel in specialized roles like SARCs and Victim Advocates.

faqs.q: Who has to complete SAPR training?
faqs.a: All military service members; DoD civilian employees typically complete related, separately structured training requirements.

faqs.q: What's the role of a SAPR Victim Advocate?
faqs.a: A Victim Advocate provides crisis intervention, support, and referrals to victims, working alongside the SARC to coordinate a victim's access to care.

faqs.q: Is Cambo affiliated with the DoD or the SAPR Office?
faqs.a: No. Cambo is an independent study tool, not produced or endorsed by the Department of Defense or the DoD Sexual Assault Prevention and Response Office.

faqs.q: Where can someone get confidential help right now?
faqs.a: The DoD Safe Helpline (1-877-995-5247, available 24/7) offers confidential, worldwide support specifically for the DoD community, separate from your chain of command.

faqs.q: Can a Restricted Report later become an Unrestricted Report?
faqs.a: Yes — a victim can convert a Restricted Report to Unrestricted at any time. The reverse isn't possible once command and/or law enforcement have been notified.
